title: eml-ice40-cybenko: code and data for Valid and False Snapping in EML Expression Trees
description: Code (eml_layer_v2.py, experiment_v2.py, basin_warmstart.py), paper source, and data for 'Valid and False Snapping in EML Expression Trees: The Basin Selection Problem'. v2.4 adds the warm-start/curriculum basin-selection note (notes/basin_selection_warmstart_note.md) with the canonical 120-row post-fix dataset (results/basin_warmstart_v2.4_postfix.csv, 20 seeds x {ln d=5, exp d=3} x {blind, warm, curriculum}): warm-start recovery 100% for exp d=3 and ln d=5, blind 25-35%, with auditable pretrain_form column and deterministic seeding. v2.5 makes ln over-depth curriculum a real curriculum via top-aligned grow_from_shallow (ln d=5 curriculum 20/20, results/basin_warmstart_v2.5_unbalanced.csv + addendum note) and adds pip-installable packaging with examples. v2.6 adds Track C hardware realization (hardware/ package): valid snapped forms from the released CSVs compile to fixed-point iCE40 FPGA RTL (combinational, pipelined EBR-based, and byte-streaming variants) with a bit-exact integer reference model, Icarus-verified bit-equality (6/6 designs), a 50-test suite, and measured UP5K synthesis numbers with valid bitstreams (ln d=4: 1964 LCs / 13 EBR / 16.7 MHz; exp d=2: 316 LCs / 3 EBR / 28.3 MHz). Includes the original 240-run v2.2 sweep CSV, the pre-fix v2.3 diagnostic corpus, and all figures. v2.7 is the Zenodo publication release: paper v2.3 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20671038) and the warm-start/curriculum technical note v1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20671272) published, figure 3 regenerated from the canonical dataset, metadata corrected. v2.8 adds a physical Lattice iCEstick (iCE40-HX1K) board demo of the exp d=2 core over a UART bridge: the host streams the 256-point sweep and the board returns bit-exact codes (256/256) matching the Python fixed-point model, with build/flash tooling, UART bring-up diagnostics, and a host-side checker.
